data.name: stakeholder_overview
data.value:
A workflow is a piece of work broken into named stages. Each stage is an activity, and the graph says where each of that activity's outcomes leads. Today each outcome leads to exactly one place — one next activity, or the end of the run. Independent pieces of analysis that share no inputs still occupy the walk one after another, and repeating the same activity over many items happens inside a single worker.

The cost is time and visibility. A run that could finish when the last of several independent pieces returns instead waits in a line. Someone watching the session sees one next step, not a set of open branches, so a fan in flight looks like a stall. The work package exists so a destination can name several branches, each with its own worker, and the walk continues from one join once the last branch returns.

data.name: classification_rationale
data.value: Inventive-improvement: nothing currently fails; the graph already routes, and the work adds a destination form that names several branches. Complexity is complex: the specification names architectural decisions (destination form, derived join, frontier, branch keys, output isolation), several viable approaches in the list-fan and instance-fan design records, and coupled changes across schema, session record, dispatch, guards, and observability. GitNexus impact on inferred symbols (next_activity, handleNextActivity, evaluateTransition, dispatch_child) returned not-found, so complexity is from the issue text and the existing specification rather than measured fan-out.

data.name: problem_statement
data.value:
A workflow graph binds each activity outcome to exactly one next activity, or to the end of the run. Independent analyses that share no inputs therefore occupy the walk one after another, and repeating one activity over a collection happens inside a single worker. A run that could finish when the last of several independent pieces returns instead waits in a line; a watcher sees one next step rather than a set of open branches.

System: the MCP server walks Goal → Workflow → Activities → Techniques → Tools. An activity names outcomes; the graph names where each leads; a worker is dispatched per activity; the session record holds the walk position. Server code lives on main; workflow definitions on the workflows branch. Guards, dispatch, the session record, and observability all read the destination as a single activity id.

Impact: High for wall-clock time and operator visibility on any workflow with independent analyses or per-item repeats. Frequency is every such walk. Unaddressed, independent work stays serial and a fan in flight looks like a stall.

Success criteria (ticket-derived, unquantified): a destination can name several branches — distinct activities, or one activity once per collection element; each branch runs in its own worker; the walk continues from one join once the last branch returns. Measurable criteria are unfilled here; they land in requirements elicitation. The specification, seven-stage delivery plan, smoke-test plan, and supersession documents already exist in the planning folder.

Constraints: implement against those documents; no backward-compatibility layers; work in the worktree at /home/mike1/projects/dev/workflow-server/.worktrees/2026-09-09-parallel-activities on branch feat/671-parallel-activities-a-graph-destination; PR #672 exists. Calendar deadline and resource limits are unfilled in the issue record. The bound issue_record carries title, number, labels, and URL, not the issue body.

Root cause: the destination type is a single activity id (or the terminal sentinel). There is no graph form for a list of members or an instance-over-collection, so independence and repetition cannot be routing facts.
